correctness.rationale: For kappa>2D_K/mu^2, the two-sided Gaussian-stiffness stochastic convolution is L2. Only shared W increments contribute to E[X0 Xt]. Exact Gaussian Var(A_u), Var(B_t), Cov(A_u,B_t) give a convergent positive integral and its beta-tilt transform. Derivative of log C yields kappa-q+q exp(-mu t)(2M_lambda(c(t))-1). M_lambda is strictly increasing since its derivative is the strictly positive tilted variance. Its endpoint values yield a unique positive root precisely for 0<lambda<1, at most one crossing and sharp endpoint cases. Analytic expansion gives the positive e^(-2mu t) critical term. Actual checker.py ran to completion with 96 independent quadrature, differentiation, sign, variance and asymptotic diagnostics. Finite tests are auxiliary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The directly motivated unknown is temporal stationary position memory for the standard continuously fluctuating OU stiffness model, whereas the cited primary source derives only single-time statistics. The natural log-correlation relaxation rate has three qualitatively distinct approach phases and a unique crossing time with an explicit threshold. At a sharp parameter surface its first exponential correction cancels and an unexpected second-harmonic rate correction emerges. This is a structural temporal classification, not a numerical threshold fit or arbitrary parameter slice, and is relevant for distinguishing noisy trapping memory from effective constant-stiffness decay. No downstream application or finite-sample feasibility is asserted.
